assertions.description: INCORRECT: The thumb cluster has KEY1..KEY6 (6 true matrix keys each with a 1N4148 diode) plus EC1 (Alps EC11 rotary encoder with integrated push switch). EC1's S1 pin connects to COL_7, but its S2 pin connects to an unnamed net (a direct MCU input, not a ROW net). The key matrix detector counts EC1 as a matrix switch because S1 touches COL_7, resulting in switches_on_matrix=7 and diodes_on_matrix=6. The true key matrix has only 6 switches. EC1's click function is wired as a direct input, not through the row-column diode matrix. The mismatch (7 switches, 6 diodes) is numerically correct but logically misleading—EC1 is not a matrix key.
assertions.migration_note: Path migrated from: signal_analysis.key_matrices[0].switches_on_matrix; TH-109 triage: {"path": "findings[0].switches_on_matrix", "op": "equals", "value": 7, "detector_filter": "detect_key_matrices"} -> {"path": "findings", "op": "contains_match", "detector_filter": "detect_key_matrices", "field": "switches_on_matrix", "pattern": "^6$"} (True matrix has 6 switches (EC1 is a direct input); the OLD aspirational check (equals 7) pinned the defect. Today switches_on_matrix=7. Lock lives in ErgoSNM_Keyboard_rev2_thumb_cluster/.../thumb_clu)
